expect.note: js-yaml (YAML 1.1 core) and `yaml` (1.2) read `no`/`on`/dates differently. The spec does not name a YAML version.
§4.1: header matched by name, 'making column reordering safe'.
A header needs ALL values non-numeric, so this is data and refs fall back to A-Z.
The heuristic eats the first data row as a header. Exports from other apps hit this often. See amendment P2 (explicit `header`).
Refs must be 'lowercase, no spaces' (§3.2), but §4 uses header values as refs. Core makes `unit_price`; the prototype keeps `Unit Price` and quotes it in formulas.
Spec does not forbid duplicates. The prototype rejects them; core keeps both and resolves to the first.
`q12` is q row 12 or q1 row 2. Spec does not forbid refs that end in digits nor give a rule.
Not all values match refs, so per A.5 it is a data row (text 'a','x' in row 1). Probably not what the author meant.
Only `-9.99` and `(9.99)` are defined. `1e3`, `.5` and `+5` are not mentioned.
§5: not parseable as the type → string + warning. Canonical storage is `.`-decimal without symbols.
Lowercase is canonical, uppercase is accepted by A.6. `True` is not defined.
Display divides by 100, but the spec does not say what `p1` is in a formula: 50 or 0.5. Excel stores 0.5. This makes `=200*p1` 10000 vs 100 — a format-level decision.
§8.1 warns that formulajs returns Date objects, but the spec does not define date values in formulas (serial number? ISO text?) nor what `d1+1` returns.
No time zone rule: is `2024-01-31T09:30:00` local or UTC? `Z` and offsets are ISO 8601 but not listed.
§6.1 says `currency` is required, but not what a reader does without it. Core falls back to USD.
Every value that starts with `=` is a formula, quoted or not. There is no way to store the text `=x` (Excel uses a leading `'`).
Excel: -2^2 = 4 and 2^3^2 = 64 (left-assoc). Sheets: 4 and 64. LibreOffice: 4 and 64. Spec gives no precedence.
Spec: `%` is modulo. Excel/Sheets/LibreOffice: `50%` = 0.5 and `7%3` is a syntax error. Imported formulas with `%` change meaning.
`&` is not in §8.6 but is one of the most used operators in real workbooks.
No `$` in the spec. Imported workbooks are full of them; fill/copy needs them.
§8.3: start and end must share the same ref, so this is invalid; Excel ranges are rectangles (VLOOKUP tables, SUMPRODUCT).
Not in the spec; spike 4–6 recommend it (one shared formula per column). Spec would read `aantal` as a def name → error.
A.10: hard error. Excel and Sheets show a per-cell circular error and keep the file open.
Excel values shown. Spec does not define blank.

Excel: `="3"+1` is 4, SUM skips text (here a1 is the number 3, a2 the text "4"), so 3. Also: CSV quoting cannot mark `3` as text in an untyped column — there is no way to store the text "007" except a `string` column type.
Excel shows 0.3 (15 significant digits) and ROUND gives 2.68. Spec does not define precision.
Excel, Sheets and LibreOffice compare text case-insensitively.
Very common in imported workbooks (`SUM(B:B)`), not in the spec.
